newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/12.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/12.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 12.0/12.5 percent on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said overnight rate was steady following a central bank supply of a modest 190 billion rupiah.
"It's quite a steady market," one local bank dealer said, adding that some operators tried to cash out from arbitrage gains with the swap market. Overnight swap was at 0.5 points.
Dealers said some operators were surprised with the jump of overnight money to 20 percent late on Monday, causing them to cover their short positions in overnight swaps in the morning.
One said some operators misjudged the market on Monday because tax payments on Friday were delayed to the next working day due to a public holiday last week.
He said weekly tax payments at mid-month were higher than usual which seemed to have caused the sudden surge.
Another dealer said one-week money was biddish as operators prepared to boost liquidity due to the approaching month-end.
However, it was quoted at 12.0 percent, down from 12.5 percent on relatively ample rupiah supply. One-month money also declined to 12.5 percent from 13.0 percent.
The central bank offered seven-day bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 12.9 percent, compared with 10.44 percent on Thursday.
Bond dealers said prices were little changed, with buying demand in Astra International shoring up its price, while PLN V A/1996 bonds edged down slightly.
They said overall interest remained steady.
